# Summary

```{r}
#| label: SummaryDevnotes
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false

classes <- xml_find_all(doc, ".//class")

# Extract <devnotes> content and class names
result <- data.frame(
  class_name = xml_attr(classes, "name"),
  devnotes   = sapply(classes, function(class_node) {
    devnotes_node <- xml_find_first(class_node, "./devnotes")
    if (!is.na(devnotes_node)) trimws(xml_text(devnotes_node)) else NA_character_
  }),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
# Find the TGrowthCurvePlant class node
class_node <- xml_find_first(doc, ".//class[@name='TGrowthCurvePlant']")

# Extract all propertyref nodes inside that class
properties <- xml_find_all(class_node, ".//propertyref")

# Extract attributes: name and visibility
property_df <- data.frame(
  name       = xml_attr(properties, "name"),
  visibility = xml_attr(properties, "visibility"),
```

```{r}
#| include: false
library(xml2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

# Load XML
#doc <- read_xml("UGrowthCurvePlant.xml")

# Find TGrowthCurvePlant class node
class_node <- xml_find_first(doc, ".//class[@name='TGrowthCurvePlant']")

# Extract <propertyref> elements
property_refs <- xml_find_all(class_node, ".//propertyref")

property_df <- data.frame(
  name       = xml_attr(property_refs, "name"),
  visibility = xml_attr(property_refs, "visibility"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)



# Extract <field> elements under <members>
#field_nodes <- xml_find_all(class_node, ".//members/field")
field_nodes <- xml_find_all(class_node, ".//field")

# Extract name, type, and optional <summary> and <remarks>
field_df <- data.frame(
  name     = xml_attr(field_nodes, "name"),
  type     = xml_attr(field_nodes, "type"),
  summary  = sapply(field_nodes, function(x) {
    summary_node <- xml_find_first(x, ".//summary")
    if (!is.na(summary_node)) xml_text(summary_node) else NA_character_
  }),
  remarks  = sapply(field_nodes, function(x) {
    remarks_node <- xml_find_first(x, ".//remarks")
    if (!is.na(remarks_node)) xml_text(remarks_node) else NA_character_
  }),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Combine property_ref and field info by matching name
full_df <- left_join(property_df, field_df, by = "name")

# Optional: clean up whitespace
full_df <- full_df %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~str_squish(.)))

# View result
#print(full_df)

```

## Descendence

The class TGrowthCurvePlantRoots is derived from TGrowthCurvePlant which derived from TSubmodel which is derived from TObject or TGraphicControl when compiled for a console app or a Delphi VCL application.

TGrowthCurvePlant \|TAbstractPlant \|\_\_\_\_TSubmodel

## Scientific Background

The class TGrowthCurvePlantRoots adds root growth functionality to the class TGrowthCurvePlant. It uses many functions from the source code file URootGrowthUtils.pas which is also used by the class TSimpleRootModDM.


## Fine-root biomass and root length

The `TGrowthCurvePlantRoots` can simulated the development of total root length either using growth curves or indirectly from the development of fine root biomass and the parameter specific root length. 

`TGrowthCurvePlantRoots` integrates `DMFineRoot` in g/m² from its ancestor TAbstractPlant. Its change is calculated from `DMFineRoot.c = max(0, DM_Change) * fFineRoot`, with `fFineRoot = max(0, fFineRoot0 - fFineRootDec * TSum)`. `TSum` is the existing base-temperature-corrected temperature sum from sowing. The defaults are `fFineRoot0 = 0.4` and `fFineRootDec = 0.0002` per degree-day. Fine-root accumulation stops at harvest; negative DM growth does not remove roots. The fitted DM curve remains unchanged. The older `TGrowthCurvePlantRootDM` subclass retains its separate `DM_Change * fFineRoot / (1 - fFineRoot)` convention.

Root ageing is an optional feature which is implemented as a simple box-car approach, i.e. after a certain duration the roots are seen as not longer effective and then are not part of the `effective root lenth` anymore.


`TGrowthCurvePlantRoots` supports these settings:

| Setting | Meaning |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `WithRoots` | Single root-growth switch inherited from `TAbstractPlant`; default `true`. Set to `false` to disable root calculations and soil-depth connections. Use this instead of the removed duplicate `OptWithRoots` option in configuration files. |
| `SRLcalc = fromGrowthcurve` | Default: use the existing logistic root-length curve. |
| `SRLcalc = fromDMfineRoot` | Calculate root length as `DMFineRoot * sp_RL / 10000` in cm/cm². |
| `sp_RL` | Specific fine-root length in cm/g DM; default 7000. |
| `Opt_RootAgeing = true` | Use the circular box-car cohorts and running active-root totals. |
| `ActiveDuration` | Number of active cohorts, truncated and bounded to 0–500. One cohort is added per `CalcRates` call, as in `TSimpleRootModDM`; daily calls give days. |
| `CalcMoments = true` | Calculate ten lognormal quantiles per layer for total and effective RLD. |
| `VK_lrv_int`, `VK_lrv_slope` | Define layer CV (%) as `max(0, VK_lrv_int + VK_lrv_slope * ln(mean RLD))`; both default to zero. |

Quantiles are normalized to preserve the layer mean. `WLD_stdev_XX` and `effWLD_stdev_XX` report their actual standard deviations. With `CalcMoments` disabled, all quantiles equal the layer mean. `SoilWaterModel.PlantModel = GrowthCurvePlantRoots1` automatically links the live total and effective moment matrices, including after initialization and crop changes. The optional `RootedSoilWaterModel` property remains available for explicit coupling. Class-resolved water uptake requires `SinkTermMethod = MFP` and `WithClasses = true` in the soil-water options. Root lengths, cohorts, and distribution outputs are cleared outside the growing season and on initialization.


## State variables

```{r}
#| label: StateVariables
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
fn <- "csv_Hume_Docu/GrowthCurvePlantRoots1.csv"
df <- read.delim(fn, header = TRUE, sep = ";", fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
df.state <- df %>% filter(Submodel == "GrowthCurvePlantRoots1", EntityType == "State") %>% dplyr::select(EntityName, Units, Value, Comment)
names(df.state) <- c("State variable", "Units", "InitialValue", "Description")
```

The class TGrowthCurvePlant has `r trunc(nrow(df.state))` following state variable(s).
